name: The growing garden
description: Cultivated rows represent the plants that can be watched closely from seedling to harvest. Calendula is one confirmed farm-grown ingredient; the map does not claim that every catalog ingredient begins here.

name: The wild edge
description: The meeting place between tended ground and surrounding plant communities is a reminder to identify carefully, ask permission, harvest lightly, and leave enough for plants, wildlife, and other gatherers.
note: Gathering practice · not a mapped boundary

name: Flowers & pollinators
description: Flowers are part crop, part habitat, and part seasonal clock. They also help identify fireweed—but Poor Louis Farms fireweed tea is made from leaves, not flowers.
note: Observation · no pollinator claim for a specific product

name: Sheep & chickens
description: Animals are included as a confirmed part of the farm story and the daily rhythm of a family place. The illustration makes no claim that animal products are sold or used in the current catalog.

name: Drying shelves
description: Airflow, humidity, temperature, and plant part all matter when moisture leaves a botanical. Drying can be a destination for tea or one step before infusing and blending.
note: Process zone · not a photograph of the workspace

name: The experiment table
description: A worktable stands for tasting, comparing, recording, and making small changes. Some experiments become products; others remain useful notes for another season.

name: The winter notebook
description: Planning continues when the garden is quiet: seeds, tools, labels, product ideas, previous results, and the ordinary logistics of the coming year.
